We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) to target molecule: SMILES given with atom mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Simplify: It's a vinyl aryl attached to a cyclobutane? Actually structure: an alkene (CH2= C(aryl) - attached to a chiral cyclobutane with OH and CF3 group). The target is likely a product of a Heck coupling between aryl bromide and alkene? The target has a phenyl attached to the alkene carbon (C2). So maybe starting from 4-bromo-1-phenyl? Actually the aryl is phenyl (c1ccccc1). So the alkene carbon attached to phenyl is sp2 carbon of alkene. Could be formed via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with an alkene (the cyclobutane alkene). The cyclobutane part: C@@H1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F. That's a cyclobutane with OH and CF3 substituents. The alkene is exocyclic: CH2= C(aryl)- attached to cyclobutane carbon (C9). So the precursor could be the same cyclobutane with a leaving group (e.g., bromide) at that carbon, then undergo Heck coupling with phenylboronic acid? Actually Heck uses aryl halide + alkene. So we need aryl halide (bromobenzene) and alkene (the cyclobutane with a double bond? Wait the target has double bond between CH2 and C attached to phenyl and cyclobutane. The cyclobutane carbon is sp2 after coupling. So the alkene precursor could be the cyclobutane with a double bond to CH2 (i.e., same as product but without phenyl). That is: [CH2]=[C]1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F (i.e., exocyclic alkene on cyclobutane). Then Heck coupling with bromobenzene to attach phenyl. So we need two precursors: the alkene (commercial?) and bromobenzene (commercial cheap). Check buyability.

Check if the alkene is commercially available: SMILES: C= C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1O? Wait need OH on cyclobutane. The cyclobutane with OH and CF3 and exocyclic alkene: SMILES maybe "C= C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1O". That is exactly the SMILES we searched earlier (C= C(Br)C1... earlier). Actually we searched C= C(Br)C1... but without Br. Let's search "C= C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1O".
